_provenance: S2.AUTHZ.XB (2026-07-27; rewritten 2026-07-28 for P2-38a/b + P3-63) — cross-boundary authz-action-set parity. Domain: approval-workflow (전자결재), specs/approval-workflow-l0.yaml (WF-AUTHZ-001..003, WF-STEP-001, WF-LIFECYCLE-001..004). THE GAP THIS FIXTURE ORIGINALLY DOCUMENTED IS NOW CLOSED: ApprovalRequestResponse carries a server-computed `allowedActions` field (P2-38b), produced by ApprovalActionEvaluator, which delegates every decision to ApprovalActionGuards — the SAME predicates ApprovalService enforces on the action path (P2-38a). So `expectedActions` is no longer hand-derived from cited guards: backend/src/test/java/.../common/AuthorizedActionSetParityTest.java now CALLS the production ApprovalActionEvaluator, and frontend/tests/authz-action-parity.vitest.ts calls the single shared selector at templates/L0/fork-receiver-kit/authorized-actions.ts, which the L4 detail page also imports (P2-39). Neutering a predicate in ApprovalActionGuards therefore flips BOTH the action-path test and this parity test — that is the mutation lock. P3-63 changed one behaviour deliberately: an approver who ACTED keeps `view` after the request goes terminal (they may see the outcome of their own decision); an assigned-but-UNACTED approver still gets nothing. The two rows below are the distinguishing pair.

rows.label: requester_draft_own_request
rows._note: Requester viewing/acting on their own DRAFT request. view: requester branch of findVisibleTo is unconditional on status (ApprovalRequestRepository.java:39-42, first OR-arm). submit/cancel: ApprovalService.loadOwn requires requesterUserId==caller (ApprovalService.java:245-251) AND the REAL ApprovalRequestStateMachine allows DRAFT->SUBMITTED and DRAFT->CANCELLED (ApprovalRequestStateMachine.java:25-26). approve/reject absent: alice is not an approver on any step here.

rows.label: approver_first_step_pending_submitted
rows._note: The assigned approver on the (only, first) PENDING step of a SUBMITTED request. view: approver branch of findVisibleTo requires status==SUBMITTED, which holds (ApprovalRequestRepository.java:39-42, second OR-arm). approve/reject: request is exactly SUBMITTED (ApprovalService.java:195-202), carol matches the step's approverUserId (ApprovalService.java:209-217), no earlier step exists so the ordering guard is vacuously satisfied (ApprovalService.java:219-227), and the REAL ApprovalStepStateMachine allows PENDING->APPROVED and PENDING->REJECTED (ApprovalStepStateMachine.java:26-27). submit/cancel absent: carol is not the requester, so loadOwn 404s (ApprovalService.java:245-251).

rows.label: non_participant_submitted
rows._note: A caller who is neither requester nor any step's approver. Deny-by-default across the board: findVisibleTo has no matching OR-arm (ApprovalRequestRepository.java:39-42) so the request is not even visible (IDOR-safe 404), and the step loop in ApprovalService.actOnStep never matches an approverUserId (ApprovalService.java:204-217) so approve/reject are unreachable regardless of request status.

rows.label: second_step_approver_visible_but_out_of_order
rows._note: THE key FE/BE-parity trap this fixture exists to pin: erin is the assigned approver of the SECOND step (orderIndex 1) of a SUBMITTED request, so she IS visible per findVisibleTo's approver OR-arm (ApprovalRequestRepository.java:39-42 does not check ordering, only status==SUBMITTED) -- a naive FE that renders an approve/reject button merely because the caller's id appears among steps[].approverUserId would show one here. But the first step (orderIndex 0, carol, still PENDING) is not APPROVED yet, so ApprovalService's strict-ordering guard rejects any action on erin's step with 409 STEP_OUT_OF_ORDER (ApprovalService.java:219-227) before the step's own state machine is ever consulted. Expected: view only.

rows.label: acted_approver_keeps_view_after_terminal
rows._note: P3-63 (narrow widening). carol APPROVED her step and the request went terminal (APPROVED). BEFORE: the visibility rule's approver arm required status==SUBMITTED, so the moment the chain completed carol lost all access — she could not see the outcome of her own decision. NOW ApprovalActionGuards.canView adds a THIRD arm: an approver whose own step carries actedByUserId == caller keeps `view` once the request is terminal. Still view-only: APPROVED is terminal in the request machine's ALLOWED map, and she is not the requester.

rows.label: unacted_approver_no_view_after_terminal
rows._note: P3-63's other half — the qualifier that keeps the widening NARROW. carol REJECTED step 0, which sent the request terminal (REJECTED) before erin (step 1) was ever asked to decide. erin is an assigned approver but her step carries no actedByUserId, so canView's third arm does not fire and she gets nothing — a rejection upstream must not retroactively disclose the request to approvers who were never reached. Paired with acted_approver_keeps_view_after_terminal, this row is what makes the widening falsifiable: drop the acted-only qualifier and THIS row goes red.

rows.label: assigned_approver_no_view_on_draft
rows._note: P3-63 negative #2 — a DRAFT has not been sent to the 결재선 yet. carol is named on step 0 but the request is still the requester's private draft, so canView gives her nothing (neither the SUBMITTED arm nor the terminal-acted arm applies). Guards against a widening that leaks unsubmitted drafts.

rows.label: requester_own_request_after_terminal_approval
rows._note: The requester viewing their own now-terminal (APPROVED) request. view: requester branch is unconditional on status (ApprovalRequestRepository.java:39-42, first OR-arm) so alice keeps visibility. submit/cancel absent: the REAL ApprovalRequestStateMachine's ALLOWED map has an empty transition set for APPROVED (ApprovalRequestStateMachine.java:29 -- terminal), so both the real markSubmitted and markCancelled calls throw IllegalStateException.
